data.narrative:
Groq is a private-stage semiconductor company that has raised $3.54B to date. The relevant comp universe consists of 3 public semiconductor peers (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private-stage competitors including Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, SambaNova Systems, Etched, and Ayar Labs.

Two standard valuation triangulation methods prove inapplicable here. Peer-median analysis fails due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables: while 12 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, none satisfy the filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier clustering (minimum 3 required). Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales multiples is also blocked—the public Semiconductors median P/S stands at 18.4x across the three tickers, but Groq's revenue is not on file, as is typical for private companies at this stage.

The absence of applicable quantitative methods reflects a structural limitation in valuing frontier-stage chip companies: the peer set is fragmented by technical differentiation and stage, while revenue disclosure remains sparse. Any valuation synthesis would require either: disclosure of Groq's revenue run rate, identification of revenue multiples within its private peer cohort, or deployment of cost-of-capital or option-value frameworks not present in the available data. The $3.54B raised provides a floor on capital deployed but does not directly imply current valuation. Further analysis depends on access to private peer financial metrics or target-specific unit economics.
